messages:
morgan: FYI — product is launching a new "Scale" quota/rate-limit multiplier next Tue. Starter tier cap drops and Scale customers get higher per-minute tokens. We need short-term capacity planning for EU + global knock-on effects.

alex: Any initial numbers? Is this expected to be a lot of GPU-hours or mostly QPS changes?

priya: did a quick sim this morning (very rough). TL;DR: behavioral shift -> more small, latency-sensitive requests. If 10% of active Pro customers opt into Scale we see ~18% increase in peak QPS and ~130k extra GPU minutes/week in eu-west-1 (~120 T GPU hours/week). US picks up ~60 T GPU hours/week.

priya: sample sim snippet:
```
scenario,eu_gpu_hours_us_gpu_hours,peak_qps_delta
base,0,0,0%
scale_10pct,120000,60000,+18%
scale_25pct,310000,150000,+45%
```

raj: :eyes: what's the tail look like? 95/99th latency? Any inference kernel regressions?

priya: 95th increases from 180ms -> 230ms in eu-west unless we adjust batch sizing or add more replicas. 99th hits ~420ms in the worst case for long-context rerank jobs. The majority of the increase is more connection churn and smaller batches (inefficient GPU utilization).

lina: Network note — pattern changes from fewer long-lived streams to lots of short connections. NLB connection tracking in eu-west-1 could become a bottleneck. Ops recommend adding +2 NLB instances and increasing conntrack limits on the NAT/edge. Also need to check our per-IP ephemeral port exhaustion on on-prem private deployments.

diego: Can we mitigate with serving changes instead of raw capacity? e.g., aggregate small requests into micro-batches at the edge, or additive KV caching for common prefixes?

priya: micro-batching helps but increases tail latency slightly; helps GPUs by ~22% utilization. KV/prefix caching helps for repeated prompts but not for single-shot varied prompts (search embeddings + rerank flow mostly unique).

morgan: Finance — are we OK with burst on-demand spend for a week while we ramp?

finance-team: short-term credit approved up to $25k for emergency burst. For anything >1 month we need a committed-reserve plan.

priya: quick cost delta (very rough):
```
option,weekly_gpu_cost
on_demand,18000
3mo_reserved_amortized,9000
```
So ~50% savings if we commit to a 3-month reserve, but requires a spend commit.

alex: Proposed path: 1) encourage Scale opt-ins on Dedicated/reserved customers (migration offer), 2) add short-term EU reserved pool + LB bump, 3) throttle starter more aggressively (backoff window) to protect SLOs, 4) SRE to enable micro-batching opt-in per-route.

raj: I'll validate autoscaling config for 95th/99th latency targets and add a safety policy to scale earlier on connection churn metrics.

lina: I'll schedule LB soak in eu-west-1 for tomorrow and post results here. Need an ops window for conntrack bump (low impact).

diego: I'll prototype edge micro-batcher and run a 2-hour perf run against the scale_10pct load generator.

morgan: Action items recap: priya -> 7-day forecast with low/med/high scenarios (include cost & GPU hour delta). lina -> LB soak + conntrack plan. raj/diego -> autoscale knobs + micro-batch test. i'll ping finance for 1-month commit approval if numbers look like mid/high.

alex: :thumbsup: let's reconvene after priya's 7-day sims.

morgan: Thanks all. Keep updates concise in this thread.
